# Known divergences: Layers

## Inline eval layers

A direct `eval` of a string literal (or of a text the layer folder computes from built-ins) is replaced by the code it runs when the code behaves the same in place. The rule, per site:

- `eval` is the global one: no binding named `eval` anywhere, no write to it, no enclosing `with`, no other sloppy direct `eval` whose text may declare `eval` in the site's function or one around it (that includes a peeled text that itself calls `eval`), and the program after the rewrite passes the built-in scan for `eval` and the folded built-ins (default lane: intact; `--unsafe`: intact or aliased).
- The text parses as a script under the strictness of the site and passes its early-error checks, every regular expression literal in it uses only the flags `gimsuy` (none twice) and passes the evaluator's own strict pattern grammar for those flags (which also refuses valid but less common syntax: lookarounds, named groups and back-references to them, `\c`, legacy octal and `\0`, `\u{...}`, property escapes, an empty class, a class escape in a range, characters outside the BMP and, under `u`, outside ASCII), has no `return`, `new.target`, `super`, `import()` or `import.meta`, and no label when the site is labelled; `await`/`yield` names are refused inside async functions and generators.
- A statement whose text declares nothing is spliced in place; one that declares only `let`/`const`/`class` is wrapped in a block. A text with `var` or function declarations is spliced only as a direct statement of a function body with simple parameters, when no other code in that function (closures included) names any declared name, the function has no other `eval` or `with`, and the names are not `arguments` or `eval`. In sloppy code the text must not `delete` a name or call `eval` (eval-declared bindings are deletable, inlined ones are not).
- A sloppy site whose text starts with `"use strict"` runs as `(() => { "use strict"; ... })()`, which keeps `this`, `arguments` and the text's own var scope. Where the site is the body of an `if`, a loop or a label, the call is wrapped in a block.
- A site inside a class field initialiser or static block, or inside an arrow function in one, is kept (there `arguments` in the text is an early error).
- An `eval` used as a value is replaced by `(0, <expression>)` when the text is one expression statement, so a function in it gets no inferred name and a member call loses its receiver as it did.
- `//# sourceURL=` and `//# sourceMappingURL=` comments in the text are dropped.

Divergences: the source text of a function that held the `eval` changes (`Function.prototype.toString`), error stacks no longer name the `sourceURL`, and the inlined code runs one frame shallower.

Premise: the text is judged by the grammar of the engine that runs the output. Syntax only some engines accept (optional chaining, private names, newer regular expression features) is inlined when it parses, so a feature test such as `try { eval("a?.b") } catch {}` loses its fallback branch on an engine without it. Regular expressions are the exception above.

## Function layers

`Function(params, body)(args)` is peeled to `(function anonymous(params) { body })(args)`. That function expression binds `anonymous` inside itself, which the function `Function` makes does not, so the layer is kept when the body names `anonymous` or contains a direct `eval` (which could read the name at run time).

Built-in scan (default lane) is an allowlist. A built-in root (`Object`, `Array`, `Function`, `Reflect`, `Symbol`, `String`, `Number`, `JSON`, `Math`, `Promise`, the other listed constructors and the fold's own roots), the global object (`globalThis`, `window`, `self`, `global`, script-level `this`) and a code runner (`eval`, `Function`, `execScript`, also read off the global object as `globalThis.eval`, and the timers and host schedulers `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, `setImmediate`, `requestAnimationFrame` (and its prefixed forms), `requestIdleCallback`, `queueMicrotask` and `postTask`, which run a text or call back with the global object as `this` in browsers) may appear only as: a call or read of a listed static member (`Object.keys`, `Array.isArray`, `Math.max`, `Symbol.iterator`, ...), a read of a listed method on its `prototype` (used as a value or through `call`/`apply`/`bind`, never called with the prototype as receiver), `new Root(...)`, a direct call of a non-runner root, a direct call of a timer whose first argument is a function (a function expression or arrow, or a local name bound only to function declarations or function expressions that is never written, is not declared in a `for`-`in` or `for`-`of` head and is not a top-level `var` or function of a classic script, which a write through the global object can rebind; `.bind(...)` and any other call result are not), `typeof`, a comparison or `instanceof`, a test, or a member of the global object that names no built-in. Allowing a root never skips what is around it: a member key, the arguments of a call, the discarded parts of a comma object and every other child expression are judged as usual, and a node kind the scan does not model is walked like any other expression. A compound or logical assignment (`+=`, `||=`, `??=`, `&&=`) reads its target, so a target that is a root or reached value counts as that value read. Any other appearance (a value, a logical/conditional/comma wrapper used as an object, `.constructor`, `["prototype"]`, `call`/`apply`/`bind` on a runner, an install-if-missing write, a top-level `var` of a built-in name in a classic script, a member write on a root) makes the program not intact. The result of a method call on a root or reached receiver is itself a reached value (`[].__proto__.valueOf()`, `globalThis.valueOf()`), except a listed static of a built-in and a global function called off the global object (`window.fetch(...)`, `this.toString()`, but not the inherited `valueOf`, which returns its receiver). A sloppy function's `this` may be the global object, so a member of it named like any built-in root or code runner (`this.Reflect`, `this.eval`) is reached too. A timer or scheduler named as a member of any receiver (`document.defaultView.setTimeout`, `o["setInterval"]`, a `const` key) is judged like the free timer: harmless only as a direct call whose first argument is a function; read as a value, destructured, or called through `call`/`apply`/`bind` or a tag it is not. A strict function whose value escapes to code the scan cannot see (an argument of any call, a value returned, thrown, yielded or awaited, an array element, a store on anything but a key of a local bound only to an object or array literal that is never reassigned, or under an `on...` key, a `call`/`apply`/`bind` of it (also through `?.`), a parameter or destructuring default, a class field, an export, or a top-level `var` or function of a classic script) may also be called with the global object as `this`, so its `this` is judged like a sloppy function's. Only a strict function the walk places keeps a strict `this`: one called directly or through `new`, the constructor of a class without `extends` (a derived constructor's `this` is whatever `super()` returns), or a function declaration or literal bound to a local name or stored on such a literal object that never escapes; a named function expression is placed only by where its value goes. Any other strict function (a class method or accessor, a method of an object the walk does not follow, a function in any other position) counts as escaping. A member named `eval`, `Function` or `execScript` on any receiver is a code runner (`document.defaultView.eval`, `e.currentTarget.Function`, a strict callback's `this.eval`), and so is a `vm` or loader runner under any receiver or destructuring key (`runInThisContext`, `runInNewContext`, `runInContext`, `compileFunction`, `module._compile`), also as a value or through `call`/`apply`/`bind`. A host module that runs code is judged by the module, not the member: an `import`, `export ... from`, `import()` or `require` of `vm`, `module`, `worker_threads`, `child_process` or `repl` (with or without `node:`), a `require` or `import()` whose specifier is not a string literal, `require` used other than as a direct call, a member read or under `typeof`, and any read of `getBuiltinModule` or `createRequire` (as a member, a free name, a destructuring key, or a name an `import` or `export ... from` takes from any module) count. `process` (the free name, read off the global object, or `require("process")`) may appear only as the object of a member read whose key is known and is not a loader, `binding`, `_linkedBinding` or `dlopen`, or under `typeof`, a comparison or a test; used as a value (`Object.values(process)`, a spread, `for`-`in`, destructuring, an argument) it counts, as do a default or namespace import of it, `import()` of it and `export * from` it. A specifier is normalised the way the URL parser does before it is judged (leading and trailing control characters and spaces dropped, tabs and newlines removed anywhere, case folded), and one with any scheme other than `node:`, `file:`, `http:` or `https:` counts like a `data:` URL. `inspector` is left to the debugger premise in the README. A window the host hands back under a plain name (`document.defaultView`, `contentWindow`, `opener`, `ownerGlobal`, an event's `currentTarget`, `target`, `srcElement`, `view` or `source`, or a local name assigned one of these) may not take a write whose key the scan cannot resolve or that names a built-in root, code runner or timer, whether by assignment, `delete`, a definer (`Object.defineProperty`, `Object.assign`, `Reflect.set` and the others, also read off such a window as `w.Object.defineProperty`) or `__defineGetter__`/`__defineSetter__`. The value of `open(...)` or of `composedPath()`, an index into either and a route read under a `const` key count as such a window too. Such a window used other than as the object of a member, a callee, the initialiser of a local name or the value assigned to one, or under `typeof`, a comparison or a test (passed as an argument, put in an array or object, returned, stored on a member) counts when the program also writes, by any of those means, a key the scan cannot resolve or one naming a built-in root, code runner or timer on a receiver it does not take for a window: such a write may land on the window it lost track of. A tagged template is a call: `` f`...` `` is judged like `f(...)`, so `` [].__proto__.valueOf`` `` is reached and `` setTimeout`...` `` runs a text. `__defineGetter__`, `__defineSetter__`, `__lookupGetter__` and `__lookupSetter__` count the same under any key spelling (`o["__defineGetter__"]`, a template literal, `?.[...]`, a literal concatenation or a `const`). Prototypes also count as reached when read under `__proto__`, `constructor`, `__lookupGetter__` or `__lookupSetter__` (as a member key, a destructuring key or a free name), through `getPrototypeOf`/`Reflect.get` on any root or reached owner, or under a computed key that is not a number, a string literal, a literal concatenation or a `const` initialised to one of these. Any `with` statement, and an `import()` or `import` of a `data:`, `blob:` or `javascript:` URL (or of a specifier that is not a literal) also count. The default lane assumes the program does not hand code text to a DOM API that evaluates it (`document.write`, a `javascript:` URL, `importScripts` of a `data:` URL, a script element's `text`, `textContent` or `src`, an event-handler attribute string or `setAttribute("on...")`). `--unsafe` assumes no built-in prototype is patched through a value the program reads; only a write whose target names the built-in (`Array.prototype.toString = ...`) is respected.

## Loader layers

A classic script whose last statement hands a computed text to the `Function` constructor or to `eval` (JSFuck, JScrewIt, jjencode, aaencode and hand-written loaders) is peeled when the evaluator can run everything before that hand-off. The program is split into a prefix (every statement before the last) and the last statement, which must be `K(A...)(B...)` (also `new K(A...)(B...)`) for `Function` or `G(A)` for `eval`. The evaluator runs the prefix, then evaluates `K` (or `G`) and every `A` in order, and the layer is peeled only when `K` is the built-in `Function` (or `G` the built-in `eval`) and every `A` is a string. A `Function` call met on the way is run exactly: the evaluator asks for its text, which must parse as `function anonymous(params\n) {\nbody\n}` without naming `anonymous`, and reruns with that function, whose source text is the one `Function` makes. A `Function` text is peeled as `(function anonymous(params) { body })(B...)` (the rule of a Function layer). An `eval` text takes the place of the call as script code, judged like an eval layer; a text that starts with `"use strict"` runs as `(() => { "use strict"; ... })()`, which keeps its own var scope.

`K` and `A` are not kept, so their evaluation must not be observable: the prefix holds no function or class, the last statement assigns no member and deletes nothing, every binding it writes is declared inside it, it runs no function from outside it, and every built-in it calls writes nothing (or, like `reverse`, writes only an object it made itself). The evaluator refuses a host value, a regular expression it does not model and a built-in it does not know, so a text built from coercions (`[]+{}`, `(![]+[])[1]`, the `[native code]` text of a built-in, `Number.prototype.toString(radix)`, `String.fromCharCode`, `escape`, the HTML methods such as `"".italics()`) is the text node computes. Not modelled, so kept: the text of the global object (JSFuck's `[`), `Date` (JSFuck's `G`, `M`, `T`), array iterators (JScrewIt's `NODE_22` features), and a JScrewIt program that calls a global through `Function("return console")()` instead of handing over a text.

The default lane keeps the prefix as it was: its writes go to globals another script could read. `--unsafe` drops it when it wrote no object that existed before it ran and called only built-ins that write nothing, no other input is given, the prefix deletes nothing and has no `for`-`in`, `for`-`of` or `with`, and the peeled text and `B` name none of the prefix's names and none of `eval`, `Function`, `globalThis`, `window`, `self`, `global`, `frames`, `top`, `parent`, `setTimeout` or `setInterval`. Premise of that drop: nothing reads the prefix's globals through the global object. The default lane also needs one closed input (with other inputs given the layer is `--unsafe` only), since another input could patch a built-in before the loader runs; `--unsafe` assumes built-ins are not patched.
